title: Croque Monsieur
description: A French ham and cheese sandwich blanketed in béchamel and broiled until the top is bubbling and golden. More indulgent than a grilled cheese, and entirely worth it.

ingredients.name: white bread
ingredients.notes: pain de mie, Pullman, or good-quality sandwich bread

ingredients.name: ham
ingredients.notes: about 8 oz, good-quality deli ham or jambon de Paris

steps.text: Melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and whisk constantly for 1 minute until the mixture smells nutty but hasn't taken on color.
steps.tip: This is a white roux — cook it just long enough to lose the raw flour taste but not so long that it browns.

steps.text: Gradually pour in the warm milk while whisking. Continue whisking until the sauce is smooth and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon, about 3 to 4 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in the nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Preheat the broiler to high. Lightly toast the bread slices under the broiler or in a toaster until just golden, about 1 minute per side.
Spread Dijon mustard on one side of 4 bread slices. Layer 2 slices of ham and a generous handful of gruyère on each. Top with the remaining bread slices.
Place the sandwiches on a sheet pan. Spoon the béchamel generously over the top of each sandwich, spreading it to the edges. Sprinkle the remaining gruyère over the béchamel.
Broil until the cheese is melted, bubbling, and deeply golden in spots, about 3 to 4 minutes. Watch closely — broilers are unforgiving. Let cool for 2 minutes before cutting.
steps.tip: For a croque madame, top each finished sandwich with a fried egg.
